## Stages

Order follows the ranking with these exceptions. O3 joins O1 in Stage 1, because downloaded indexes are not a usable result until they are parsed. O9 comes before O7 and O10, because reconciliation publishes through generations. O4 and O11 move to Stage 6, because the Azure platform deploys code that does not exist yet and is sized from Stage 1's measured cost. O1, O2 and O7 reach production standard in Stage 7.

      Consumes: an SEC User-Agent identity and a quarter range supplied by you; nothing built
      Produces: a throttled single-process downloader, raw snapshots stored by SHA-256, the sec-index-v1 parser and Parquet writer (§4.5), and specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1: every quarter in the range is downloaded, validated per §4.3 and stored by hash, with no HTML or truncated body accepted. O3: canonical rows for those quarters are in Parquet with unique `(cik, archive_path)` keys. Cost: the findings file records, per quarter, bytes, rows, elapsed time, peak memory and observed request rate (at or below 3 req/s).
      Leaves out: daily discovery: Stage 2; source manifest and replay: Stage 3; shared request lease: Stage 3; versioned publication: Stage 4; reconciliation: Stage 5; Azure deployment and full config validation: Stage 6; full-range golden fixtures, scheduling, monitoring and alerts, runbooks: Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

      ROUTING: writing-plans

      Objective: Make source, snapshot, processing and attempt state durable, so that runs resume and replay from raw storage, and make every collector share one request budget.

      Exit: O6: the §6 "Replay" tests pass, including a parser-version rebuild with SEC access disabled. O8: the §6 "Access" tests pass.
